name: Battle of the Trebia
note: The Carthaginian camp lay west of the Trebia and the Roman camp east of it, so north is drawn at the top; the accounts do not say which way the river ran, and it is drawn straight. The fight was on the flood plain west of the river. The accounts do not say in which direction Placentia lay. The Carthaginian elephants stood beyond each block of veteran infantry and are not drawn. The Carthaginian light infantry went round both Roman flanks and the Roman velites faced them; the plan shows that as one move on the southern side. The Gallic allies on the Roman side, and the Gallic and Numidian parts of the Carthaginian cavalry, are not set apart, because the accounts do not say where they stood. The paths of the cavalry are drawn straight.

phases.title: The Numidians provoke the Romans
phases.when: Shortly before daybreak, 22 or 23 December 218 BCE
phases.text: Hannibal sent his Numidian cavalry across the river to force back the Roman pickets and provoke a fight. Mago had already taken 1,000 cavalry and 1,000 infantry in the night to an old watercourse, where they hid.
phases.quote: Shortly before daybreak Hannibal sent his Numidian cavalry across the river to force back the Roman pickets and provoke a fight.

phases.title: The Romans ford the Trebia after the Numidians
phases.text: Sempronius sent out his cavalry, then the velites and then the whole army. The Numidians drew back slowly, and the Romans followed them through the icy, chest-high water of the Trebia.
phases.quote: The Numidians withdrew slowly and Sempronius pushed his whole army after them

phases.title: The armies form up on the west bank
phases.text: The Romans organised themselves in battle formation west of the Trebia, facing the Carthaginian army, which had formed up symmetrically. The light infantry of both sides stood between the lines. Mago's force lay hidden in a watercourse to the south.
phases.quote: The Carthaginian army formed up symmetrically: the 8,000 Gallic infantry were in the centre;

phases.title: The Carthaginian skirmishers drive back the velites
phases.text: The velites had used many javelins against the cavalry and were unfed, tired and cold, while the Carthaginian slingers outranged them. The Carthaginians got the better of the skirmishing and drove the velites back through the gaps in their heavy infantry.
phases.quote: For these reasons the Carthaginians got the better of the initial skirmishing and drove the velites back through the gaps in their supporting heavy infantry.

phases.title: The skirmishers harass the Roman cavalry
phases.text: The Carthaginian light infantry moved towards the flanks of their army and harassed the Roman cavalry with their missiles. The Roman horses were already tired from chasing the Numidians.
phases.quote: The Carthaginian light infantry then moved towards the flanks of their army and harassed the Roman cavalry with their missiles

phases.title: The Roman cavalry flees and the infantry lines close
phases.text: On each wing 5,000 Carthaginian horse charged the 2,000 Roman horse, which fled back over the Trebia. Most of the Carthaginian cavalry pursued them while the heavy infantry lines met in the centre. The skirmishers fell back behind their cavalry.
phases.quote: Both encounters ended rapidly, with the Romans fleeing back over the Trebia and most of the Carthaginian cavalry pursuing them.

phases.title: Carthaginian skirmishers go round the exposed flank
phases.text: The Carthaginian light infantry moved forward and round the Roman flank, which the flight of the cavalry had left open. The velites turned to face them and many allied infantry on the flanks turned too, which slowed their push on the front.
phases.quote: The Carthaginian light infantry, who had withdrawn to the wings behind the cavalry, moved forward and round the now exposed Roman flanks.

phases.title: Mago's force strikes the Roman left rear
phases.text: Mago's men came down the watercourse unnoticed and charged the velites, who were already holding off the Carthaginian light infantry. The velites held their formation.
phases.quote: Mago's force charged into the velites who were already fending off the Carthaginian light infantry, but their formation held.

phases.title: The Carthaginian cavalry returns to the Roman rear
phases.text: Increasing numbers of Carthaginian cavalry broke off the pursuit, came back and attacked the Roman rear. Under this strain the allied infantry on the flanks and the velites began to break up.
phases.quote: Increasing numbers of Carthaginian cavalry broke off their pursuit, returned and attacked the Roman rear.

phases.title: The Roman centre breaks through the Gauls
phases.text: The Roman infantry in the centre routed the 8,000 Gauls facing them and broke through the middle of the Carthaginian army. Behind them the rest of the Roman army had dissolved.
phases.quote: Meanwhile, the Roman infantry in the centre routed the 8,000 Gauls facing them, as well as a unit of African heavy infantry, and broke clean through the centre of the Carthaginian army.

phases.title: Ten thousand Romans reach Placentia
phases.text: Sempronius ordered the infantry away from the field. Keeping its formation, 10,000 of them recrossed the Trebia and reached Placentia. The Carthaginians cut down the partly surrounded rest of the Roman army.
phases.quote: The Carthaginians concentrated on pursuing and cutting down the partially surrounded balance of the Roman army.
